text: A resident pushes her tray of grey mash away again. "Not hungry, dear." {boss} taps a watch.
A resident's son slips you a fat envelope. "For looking after Dad." Policy says no gifts.
A ward is demanding a bed that does not exist. {boss} says find one. The corridor is empty.
{friend} knows a shortcut through the loading bay. Saves ten minutes. The door says staff only.
Three call bells ring at once. {rival} is on break. Again. Their coffee is still steaming.
{friend} offers to show you how to take blood. They grin. "Don't faint. The last one fainted."
The sat nav says left. {friend} says right. The siren screams. Someone out there isn't breathing.
You did everything right, by the book. It wasn't enough. Nobody turns the radio on for the drive back.
You glance at the chart and freeze. {rival} wrote ten times the dose. The patient hasn't had it yet.
Fourth night shift in a row. The vending machine is out of crisps. {crush} brings you a coffee at 4am.
The prescription looks off. The signature's wrong, the ink still wet. The man drums on the counter.
An old man tips twelve pill bottles onto the counter. He asks if he really needs all of them.
A kid in the chair bites {boss}'s finger and won't let go. {boss} squeaks. Everyone looks at you.
{rival} is spreading a rumour about you and {crush}. The receptionist winks at you. Twice.
{boss} wants more veneers sold. Your patient has perfectly good teeth and trusts you completely.
Years of leaning over chairs, peering into mouths. Your back clicks when you stand. It's complaining.
Midnight. A farmer's cow is calving badly in a muddy shed. It's raining sideways.
A man counts coins onto the counter for his cat's surgery. He counts twice. He's short.
Everyone says it's a virus and the bed is needed. Something about the rash bothers you.
Hour 30 of your shift. You've read the same chart three times. The coffee went cold hours ago.
Your regular client cancels for the third week. The text is short, no emoji. They always use emoji.
{boss} flicks through your notes, stopping on a page with one line. "These are... thin."
It's scorching. The steel burns to touch. {boss} wants the slab poured before lunch.
The frame's a few millimetres out. The bubble sits just off centre, smugly. Nobody would ever know.
{boss} swears the circuit's dead and reaches for the wires. Your tester beeps red. It disagrees.
The new apprentice has wired the switch upside down. Up is off. They are beaming with pride.
3am. Burst pipe, water through the ceiling. The caller is crying too hard to say the address.
You pull a clump of hair and soap out of the drain. Something glints. A diamond ring, slimy and real.
Hammer. Thumb. You make a noise you didn't know you could. {rival} laughs so hard they sit down.
The stairs are due Friday. It's Thursday. Right now they're a pile of planks and a doodle.
{boss} wants you to tell an old lady she needs new brakes. She doesn't. She offers you a biscuit.
"It makes a noise." That's all the customer says. Then they make a vague whooshing face.
Forty covers at once. {boss} is shouting. {rival} has burnt the risotto. The smoke alarm wonders.
The steak slides off the tongs and slaps the floor. You look around. Nobody saw. It's an expensive steak.
Hour fourteen at the wheel. The radio is static and the white lines are starting to dance.
A soaked hitchhiker on the verge, cardboard sign melting in the rain. Company rules say no.
Third dry month. The fields look like toast. The water tank clangs hollow when you knock it.
A calf is coming backwards. It's 2am, the shed light flickers and {friend} is asleep in the house.
The office party ended at midnight. There's cake on the ceiling and a shoe in a plant pot. You start at 5.
A diamond ring, behind the toilet in a rich client's marble bathroom. The house is silent.
The scanner beeps: you're 12% under quota. Your feet ache. {boss} is watching your number on the big screen.
{rival} reverses the forklift into a pallet of TVs. Crunch. Tinkle. Then they turn and point at you.
The printer jams again and eats a page with a grinding noise. {boss} looks straight at you.
Two directors booked the same room for the same hour. Both stand at the door. Both booked it first.
Last day of the month. You're one sale short of quota. The office is emptying. The phone is right there.
{rival} is about to close YOUR client, using the lead from your notes. And your jokes.
Your till is twenty short at close. You count it three times. Nobody's watching the cameras.
A frail old woman wants all her savings in cash. Her "grandson" waits outside, engine running.
A young family needs a loan. The baby chews your pen. Their numbers are... hopeful.
Bonus season. {rival} leaves their letter open on the desk. Their bonus is bigger than yours. Much.
Tax season. Your inbox has 214 unread, half marked urgent. It's 9pm and your eyes itch.
A client hands you receipts for a jet ski and a pony. They want you to get 'creative' with expenses.
The filing deadline is 5pm. It's 4:40. The courier texts you a photo of a traffic jam.
{boss} presents your research to the partners as their own. Coffee stain and all. They're impressed.
Your client leans in and whispers, off the record, that they did it. Then asks how the case is going.
{boss} wants 2,000 billable hours this year. You're on track for 1,600, counting naps at your desk.
Friday, 5:55pm. The website is down. Your last change went in at 5:50. The phones start ringing.
{rival} leaves 47 comments on your code review. Most are about spacing. One just says "hmm".
Ticket #4,112: 'computer broken. URGENT.' You climb three floors. It's unplugged. They're watching.
The server upgrade has to happen overnight. Someone has to stay with the humming racks and cold pizza.
{boss} wants the new campaign to 'go viral', like the cat videos. Budget: zero. {boss} is thrilled.
Pitch meeting in ten minutes. Through the glass, {rival} is rehearsing your idea, word for word.
Ninety essays on the same poem. Sunday night, cold tea. Essay forty-one compares it to a sandwich.
A parent tells {boss} their kid "deserved an A". The kid copied half of it. {boss} wants a word.
You pull over a speeder. It's {friend}'s mother. She's already crying and offering you a muffin.
{rival} slides cash from an evidence bag into his jacket. He looks up. He sees you see it.
Smoke pours from the upstairs windows. Neighbours in dressing gowns. Someone screams there's a dog inside.
{friend} signs you up for the charity calendar. Shirtless. Holding a hose. The fan is already on.
A toddler bites another toddler. Then looks at you. Then, holding eye contact, bites again.
Twelve kids, all asleep at once on little mats. It's never happened before. You don't dare breathe.
A customer wants a refund on a toaster. It's full of water. There's a rubber duck in the slot.
An old man in a thin coat slips a tin of soup into his pocket. His hands are shaking.
{rival} posts their latte art: a swan, wings spread, perfect neck. It's annoyingly good.
Your 7am regular hasn't come in for a week. Today she's back, red-eyed, gripping her purse.
The client wants the logo bigger. And the other logo bigger. And both to pop. By voice note.
{rival} clicks to the next slide. It's your poster, your hidden doodle and all. "So I made this."
A brown envelope on your desk, no name. Inside: the mayor's expenses. All of them. Even the hot tub.
The police want your source's name, and they're not asking nicely. Your source is {friend}.
Orders come in, stamped and stapled. Your unit deploys next month. The barracks goes very quiet.
5am drill in freezing rain, boots full of water. {rival} is slacking at the back, hiding.
{boss} hands you a list of your team in a cheerful font. Cut three names by Friday.
The board wants growth this quarter. Twelve suits wait for your slide. The numbers say no.
{boss} wants everyone running hills at 6 a.m. before school. It's dark, the grass is wet and cold.
Your ankle rolls under you in a pack. You hop out. It's swelling like a balloon in your sock.
{rival} and you both play wing. There's one spot on the sheet this week. You both eye the clipboard.
Your family's on canteen duty, selling pies. They cheer very loudly at every mark you take.
{boss} hands you a laminated gym program. It is mostly squats. The last page just says "SQUATS".
You get collected in a marking contest. The sky spins. The lights look funny. There are two umpires.
The rep team list goes up on the clubroom door. Kids crowd in. Your heart is thumping.
Rep carnival interstate. Four nights in a cheap motel with the squad and one very tired manager.
{rival} is telling the scouts you can't kick on your left. Loudly. Next to the canteen.
A recruiter sits in the stands with a little notebook. Every time you touch the ball, the pen moves.
Draft combine. Clipboards and stopwatches everywhere. They time everything, even how you breathe.
A journalist pushes a microphone at you. Cameras click. Which club would you love to be drafted to?
New tyres cost more than your parents' car payment. Your old ones are bald and shiny. Race is Sunday.
Lights out. Twelve karts scream towards one tight first corner. There's a gap. Nearly a gap.
A local tiling company might put its logo on your helmet. The logo is a smiling tile with arms.
Through the kitchen door you hear your parents, quietly, about the house and your racing.
{rival} is in the same team, same kart, and half a second quicker. The timesheet gloats.
{boss} says your neck wobbles in the corners. There's a harness with weights. It looks medieval.
The engine goes bang on lap three. Blue smoke, a rattle, silence. That was expensive.
A sim rig would let you learn every track from your bedroom. Wheel, pedals, bolted seat. Small bedroom.
Last race of the regional season. You lead by two points. Second place is close enough to read your stickers.
Rain, 140 km/h, spray everywhere. The kart twitches. The barrier is coming up fast.
A real single-seater team offers a test day. Real car, real track. You pay for the fuel. All of it.
{boss} has a seat for next season. The budget is more than your house. Your parents go quiet.
{boss} blows the whistle. Suicides until someone throws up. The gym smells of sweat and polish.
You land wrong on a rebound. Your knee makes a noise like snapping celery. The gym goes quiet.
{rival} never passes. Ever. Not even when you're wide open, waving like you're landing a plane.
Down by one, no time left. Two free throws. The gym is silent. Somebody drops a juice box.
You've never dunked. Now it's a breakaway, nobody between you and the hoop, and the crowd is up.
Everyone on the team has the new signature shoes but you. Yours have tape on the toe.
There's a summer shooting camp with real coaches. It costs a lot of mowing money. A lot of lawns.
State squad trials. Two hundred kids in bibs, fifteen spots, coaches frowning in the stands.
You made state. You've played four minutes all tournament. Your warm-up top has never been warmer.
A college scout messages you. They love your game. Their account has eleven followers and no photo.
A real college flies you out. Big arena, free hoodie, a chocolate fountain. Everything is free.
{rival} got the same college offer. One scholarship left. You pass at practice without a word.
The band needs a name. {rival} wants "Mouldy Toast". They've already drawn the logo. It has a face.
The neighbour has called about the drums again. Third time this week. He's waving the phone at you.
First gig. Nine people in the room, and four are your family. Your nan brought a sign.
2 a.m. A song is half-written in your notes app. One verse is just "something about rain".
Your cover of an old song is doing numbers. Small numbers, but numbers. Someone wrote "this slaps".
Battle of the bands in a sticky hall. The prize is studio time. The last band had a smoke machine.
{rival} wants a guitar solo in every song. Every one. Even the slow one about your nan's dog.
A man in sunglasses wants to be your manager. Indoors. At night. His business cards are handwritten.
A pub gig pays real money. The stage is two pallets. You're technically too young to be inside.
An old post of yours resurfaces, screenshotted and shared everywhere. It is very, very bad.
The label wants a second demo by Friday. It's Tuesday. The drummer has a cold.
The label wants you. Just you. Not the band. The band is outside, eating chips, waiting.
Background extra. Your job is to walk past a café with an empty cup. Forty times. Again.
Audition. You pour your heart out. The casting director eats soup the whole time and slurps the sad bit.
Your agent winces at your headshots. They look like a school photo. Bad fringe and everything.
{rival} got the callback you wanted. Now they're holding out the script, asking you to run lines.
The director needs you to cry on cue. Now. Thirty crew are waiting and the light is fading.
The shoot runs into exam week. The schedule and your revision timetable overlap on the fridge.
You're cast in a yoghurt ad. One line: "Mmm". You must say it convincingly, with a spoon, eleven takes.
Someone in the cereal aisle points: "Yoghurt kid!" Three people turn round. One is holding yoghurt.
A gossip page says you were rude to a fan. You weren't. Mostly. You were hungry and had a cold.
TV bit part. You have three lines, and one is "Look out!" You've said it in the mirror two hundred times.
Your co-star is {crush}. The director wants more chemistry. The whole set pretends not to watch.
Your agent wants you to change your name. And your nose. They say it casually, buttering a roll.
{boss} says watch the corner. Whistle if you see blue. The streetlight buzzes. Your phone is on 12%.
{boss} hands you a taped-up bag, heavier than it looks. "Don't open it. Don't drop it."
Kids at school whisper when you walk past. Some move seats at lunch. A teacher stares a bit too long.
Your mum finds a roll of cash in your sock drawer. She's standing in your doorway, holding it up.
{boss} wants the servo's back door left unlocked tonight. The owner always gives you free slushies.
A police officer stops you on the way home, notebook out. "Know anything about the servo?"
You count the takings twice. {rival} has been skimming. Their new trainers are very white.
{rival} told {boss} the missing money was you. {boss} is staring at you. Nobody is talking.
You're a runner now. {boss} tosses you keys to a car with a cracked windscreen. You're fifteen.
{friend} knows a youth worker who can get you an apprenticeship. Real pay. Away from all this.
To be crew, {boss} says you need to prove yourself. Tonight. The others watch from the bench.
Squad cars keep cruising your street, slowly, every hour. Curtains twitch. {boss} says lie low.
The big bowl. Tail on the edge, toes over nothing. Everyone's watching. {friend} says just commit.
Security says the plaza isn't a skatepark. Perfect ledges, smooth stairs. It's a very good skatepark.
{friend} has a camera and a plan. You need one clip that isn't a slam. The battery's on one bar.
Your deck snapped clean in half like a biscuit. A new one costs ninety. You have about six.
{rival} lands your trick. Your trick. On your ledge. Then they do a little bow.
Your parents watched one video of you falling down stairs. Just one. They have opinions. And leaflets.
{boss} from the skate shop offers you free wheels every month. Flow, they call it.
Am contest. Two minutes, one run, three judges with clipboards and sunburn. The crowd is loud.
Team tour. Eight skaters, one van, no air con. The windows only open halfway. It smells already.
{boss} wants to put your name on a board. An actual board, on the shop wall, for sale.
Five ranked losses in a row. Your hands are sweaty. One more and you drop a tier.
Your back hurts after every session. A real gaming chair costs two hundred and fifty. You're on a stool.
A stranger in chat has thoughts about your mother. Many thoughts. All caps, bad spelling.
{friend} says you should stream. Eleven people would watch. Maybe twelve, if your nan logs on.
Your parents cut the wifi at 10 p.m. Scrims start at 10:30. Your team is already in voice chat.
{rival} is on a secret account, farming low ranks and laughing about it. The victims are about twelve.
An academy team wants a tryout. {boss} is right behind you, watching every click.
Your wrist clicks when you click. Every single time. You hear it in your sleep. That seems bad.
First LAN final. Real stage, real lights, and a trophy shaped like a sword. Your mouse hand shakes.
{boss} offers a pro contract. Gaming house, salary, a chef who only makes pasta. School's not done.
